slip.fine: The estimate changes as the pool fills and is final when betting closes. 2% fee included. Refund if there is no opposing ticket.
slip.rulesBody: Betting is open only before R1 starts, for {seconds} seconds; it is closed between rounds. Each market pays from its own pool and settles once when the match ends. A one-sided pool, or one without a winner, is refunded without a fee. Even with a correct pick the return can be less than your stake. One ticket per market per match. A dropped connection does not cancel a ticket. Punches and kicks decide the result under the same rules.

slip.emptyClosed: You have no ticket on this match. Betting is open for {seconds} s before R1 of every match.
slip.indicatorNote: “Ahead / behind” is only an indicator. The result is final when the match ends.

technical.p1: A match is at most three rounds: 30 seconds of betting, 45 seconds per round, a short break between them. A fighter who takes clean punches or kicks to the head in a row goes down; the referee counts. A fighter whose health runs out, or who goes down a third time in one round, is stopped and the match ends. Without a stoppage a round is won on the damage dealt plus 120 points for every knockdown; the fighter who wins more rounds takes the match, and a tie is a draw. Health +250 and stamina +350 carry into the next round. Techniques: jab, cross, hook, uppercut, body hook; front kick (teep), low, body and head kick; knee and clinch.
technical.p2: The seeds of all three rounds are drawn before the match starts; their hashes are published before betting opens, and each seed is revealed when its round starts. Your browser also replays the earlier rounds from the published log and checks the match result. This is not a VRF or an operator-independent proof of the result.
technical.p3: Each fighter has its own independent brain. It chooses every move itself and looks only at the match data everyone can see: the round, the time, both fighters' health and stamina, and what the opponent has done so far. A fighter keeps what it learns from round to round across the match; the rule and the initial weights are frozen when the match starts, and the same seed and log reproduce the same match. Whether this helps is tested separately and the measured result is shown on the page. Measured effect (pre-registered test, 200 matches): over a whole match, the fighter that learns is on average +38 points ahead of its non-learning copy against learning opponents (95% interval −2…+74) and +20 against fixed-style opponents (−5…+45). Because the intervals include zero, the benefit is not considered proven. The effect of training itself is clear (+284). The fly connectome structure could not be shown to beat a shuffled network.
technical.p4: Every 9 seconds the corner coach Jev (a deterministic fallback on timeout) suggests an intent, a target and a threat; the fighter reads it only as an input. Because the plans arrive after betting has closed, this game is DEMO-only. The picture is drawn in code (skeleton, IK, step planner); camera, FPS and sound do not affect the result.
